regions.name: West

regions.geography: CO, TX, UT (10-K segment): Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Colorado and Utah divisions (5 divisions)

regions.geography: DC, FL, MD, NC, SC, VA, plus GA via Coastal Carolinas (10-K segment): DC Metro, Charlotte, Raleigh, Coastal Carolinas and Orlando divisions (5 divisions)

profile.org_note: West, Central and East are 10-K reporting segments (also used as the company's own 'geographic region' grouping in its Sept 2026 overview), not management layers: no regional, area or group president exists in any 2025-2026 company source, and 16 division presidents running 17 divisions (Washington and Utah share one) sit directly under the Executive Leadership Team, most likely President and COO Tom Mitchell (inferred). Land deals are prepared by the divisions and approved centrally: the Management Land Committee (CEO Bauer, President Mitchell, CFO Keeler) reviews deals up to $50M; pre-merger, a board Executive Land Committee (directors Burrows, Gilbert, Grahl, all of whom left the board at the May 2026 Sumitomo Forestry closing) took $50M-$100M and the full board $100M+; the post-merger path above $50M is not published. No corporate land head, treasurer or capital-markets head is named; CFO Glenn Keeler signs bank and SEC documents.
profile.summary: Top-20 US builder: 4,947 deliveries and $3.36B of home sales revenue in 2025, 17 divisions in 13 states plus DC, and 32,444 lots owned or controlled at 2026-09-30 (16,683 owned, 15,761 controlled, about 49% controlled, per the Q3 2026 results release). Sumitomo Forestry bought it for $47.00 per share in cash (about $4.5B) on 2026-05-14; it is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry America, delisted from the NYSE but still filing 10-Qs because its 2027 and 2028 senior notes remain outstanding. Founders Doug Bauer (CEO) and Tom Mitchell (President and COO) stayed on, and with CFO Glenn Keeler they form the committee that approves land deals.
